keyPoint: Congress cannot restrict freedom of religion, speech, the press, assembly, or petition.
The people have the right to keep and bear arms.
Soldiers cannot be quartered in a private home in peacetime without the owner's consent.
No unreasonable searches or seizures; warrants require probable cause.
No one can be forced to testify against themselves or be deprived of life, liberty, or property without due process.
The accused has the right to a speedy, public trial by an impartial jury and to legal counsel.
The right to a jury trial is preserved in civil cases over a certain value.
Excessive bail, excessive fines, and cruel and unusual punishment are prohibited.
Rights not listed in the Constitution are still retained by the people.
Powers not given to the federal government are reserved to the states or the people.
Slavery and involuntary servitude are abolished, except as punishment for a crime.
All persons born or naturalized in the U.S. are citizens and are guaranteed equal protection of the laws.
The right to vote cannot be denied because of race or previous servitude.
The right to vote cannot be denied because of sex.
A president may be elected to no more than two terms.
The right to vote cannot be denied to citizens who are 18 or older because of age.
